clue.text: Bird's egg producing plant

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
to egg someone on is to spur them on

explanation.surface: A bird's egg somehow gives rise to a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Bird's joins the two parts, like 'has'. 'egg' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb, 'urge on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The larkspur is a garden flower, a delphinium relative with spurred blooms.

clue.text: Put two heads together, being cunning

parts.note: arch- as a prefix means chief, the head one, the first of two heads
a ness is a headland, the second head, set beside the first

explanation.surface: Two people confer and are crafty about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'heads' are ARCH (chief, as in archbishop) and NESS (a headland, as in Loch Ness's shores or Dungeness), put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is knowing slyness, a mischievous cleverness of manner.

clue.text: A stunner seen briefly in Breakout

parts.note: the short form KO, used for a stunning blow in boxing, sits inside the word Breakout

explanation.surface: Someone striking is glimpsed in a film called Breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the abbreviation KO, which appears in breaKOut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner is a dazzling person or thing, as is a knockout in informal usage, and both also mean a stunning punch.

clue.text: Poll pear-tree periodically

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, the first, third, fifth and seventh of pear-tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to prune or lop a pear tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like a verb (to pollard a tree), but it is the old noun for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old words for the head, poll as in 'poll tax', a charge per head.

clue.text: Seemingly have more qualms about fortification

definitions.meaning: a small enclosed outwork of a fort

explanation.surface: Someone has growing doubts about a military stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' flags that the word only looks like re- plus doubt; it isn't really built that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary or outlying defensive earthwork, one kind of fortification.

clue.text: Caught (ahem!) well criminally parking? You could get this

indicators.note: doing something criminally suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone, clearing their throat, is told they could be penalised for parking badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminally' rearranges C, AHEM, WELL and P together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel clamp is a device fixed to an illegally parked car, the penalty you could get.

clue.text: Rest a bit, gathering energy, having bowled first

indicators.note: having the letter for bowled come first puts it at the front

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: one word gathering another takes it inside itself

parts.note: rather means somewhat, a bit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cricketer takes a quick rest to regain energy after bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' puts E inside RATHER to make REATHER; 'first' puts B in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause to rest and catch your breath.

clue.text: I attempt emphatically to restrain the Parisian's adoration

indicators.note: restraining something means holding it within, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: an emphatic way of saying I attempt is 'I do try'
la is French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are trying to hold back their admiration for a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I attempt emphatically' is the emphatic 'I do try'; 'the Parisian' is French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive worship or devotion, adoration taken to extremes.

clue.text: Close to broke and left overdrawn apparently? He wasn't ready!

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the readies is slang for cash, so a man with an empty bank account has no ready money; the English king called the Unready seems to be one such man

indicators.note: overdrawn means in the red, so the letter for left is apparently put in the phrase

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red; 'the red' holds the next piece

explanation.surface: A man nearly bankrupt and in debt was caught unprepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Overdrawn means 'in the red', so L is put in THE RED. The definition plays on the Anglo-Saxon king's nickname, the Unready.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon king nicknamed the Unready, so he is the man who wasn't ready.

clue.text: Confronted journalist on expense account first

indicators.note: account comes first in the build, before the other pieces
in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y

parts.note: an expense is a cost
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter challenged someone about their expense claims.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; ED for editor is a standard crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and confront them boldly.

clue.text: Service he performs with valour

indicators.note: the letters perform, acting out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier serving with bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performs' is the anagram signal: HE and VALOUR together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Servicing a car or machine means overhauling it, a full check and repair.

clue.text: Greek writer cut short another writer, being intolerant

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its last letter

parts.note: Xenophon was an ancient Greek historian
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A Greek author rudely interrupts a rival out of intolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last N from XENOPHON. A 'writer' is here a pen, the brand Bic.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobic means hostile to foreigners, a form of intolerance.

clue.text: The dogs ran off, being self-willed

indicators.note: letters that go off run wild, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: The dogs ran off because they were wilful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges THE DOGS RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Headstrong means stubbornly determined to have one's own way.

clue.text: Husband's captivated by pet rabbit

indicators.note: a thing captivated by another is held inside it

parts.note: a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: A husband is charmed by the family's pet rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for talking at length (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork', talk), so it is a verb here, not the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is to talk idly, which is to chat.

clue.text: Drunkenly wandering? Butt out here!

indicators.note: a drunk slurs s into sh, so one letter is swapped for a slurred pair

parts.note: to go astray is to wander off course

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering about is told to put out a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a drunken slur, 'astray' becomes 'ashtray'. 'Butt out here' reads as 'go away', but it is where you stub out a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is the dish where a cigarette butt is stubbed out.

clue.text: Mass confusion about keeping fit? The opposite

indicators.note: keeping one thing means holding it within another
this reverses the stated container, so the fit holds the confusion rather than the other way round

parts.note: fit means able, capable

indicators.note: here about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Widespread disorder over the issue of fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as a noun but is the verb, to gather. 'The opposite' flips 'keeping': the fit holds the confusion, not the confusion the fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To mass is to gather together in a crowd, which is to come together as a group.

clue.text: Barbarian has a bit of a shock for Diana?

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders
a shock of hair is a mass of it, and a tress is a lock

explanation.surface: A wild man gives the princess a bit of a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a thick mass of hair, not a fright. Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting, not the princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt, the archetypal woman who hunts.

clue.text: We hear innocent sort's a victim and a sucker

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the letters follow a sound

parts.note: a lamb is an innocent sort, and a victim is prey: lamb prey

explanation.surface: An innocent person is described as both a victim and a dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' looks like a gullible person, but it is the fish's sucking mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that feeds by sucking blood through a round mouth.

clue.text: After drink, young boxers perhaps shouldn't start fights

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the drink

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink

indicators.note: a word that must not start loses its first letter

parts.note: young dogs, such as boxer puppies, are pups

explanation.surface: Junior boxers are told not to start brawls after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers are a dog breed, so their young are PUPS; 'shouldn't start' drops the first P to leave UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch-ups are informal British fist fights or brawls.

clue.text: Being cold previously, settle comfortably

parts.note: ens is the philosophers' Latin term for being or existence
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
once means formerly, previously

explanation.surface: Having once been cold, someone gets cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce yourself is to settle snugly in a safe, comfortable place.

clue.text: Harry is wrong about me, note

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Harry insists the note about him is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the verb 'to harass', not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them persistently, to torment them.

clue.text: Lied, perhaps, about cracking case of shoplifting

indicators.note: cracking something open means getting inside it
the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone lied about solving a shoplifting case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lied' is the German art song, not the past tense of lie; 'perhaps' says it is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, so an example of a song.

clue.text: Cut trees in a couple of seconds, showing lack of care

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, and a couple gives two
to lop is to cut off branches
pines are trees

explanation.surface: Felling trees in a hurry shows carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of seconds' gives two S's, one either side of the cut trees; 'showing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppiness is careless, untidy work, a lack of care.

clue.text: Major changes after a month — an addition to season?

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the month

parts.note: MAR is short for March

indicators.note: the word changes, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army major alters things after a month away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' means to flavour food, not a time of year; 'Major' is the anagram fodder, not a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is a culinary herb, something added to season a dish; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Cheese is abandoned by scary female writer

indicators.note: one thing abandoned by another loses that part

parts.note: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese
a gorgon is a fearsome woman, from the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A scary woman walks out on some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is abandoned by' takes GORGON out of GORGONZOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was the French novelist who wrote Germinal.

clue.text: Well-spoken European set about man heartlessly

indicators.note: one piece set about another goes round it

parts.note: a lot is a set of items, as at auction

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter is removed

parts.note: in chess the pieces are men, and the queen is one

explanation.surface: A European is articulate about a man who has no feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece, here the most powerful one; 'heartlessly' removes its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent means fluent and persuasive in speech, well-spoken.

clue.text: Sadly this extremely likeable inn has no hot tap

indicators.note: things gone sadly are in a bad way, so the letters are rearranged
the pool of letters has no letter for hot, so it is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pleasant inn is sadly without hot running water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' drops H from THIS to leave TIS; 'extremely' takes LE from likeable; 'Sadly' rearranges TIS, LE and INN together. 'tap' is phone-tapping, not plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a phone is to eavesdrop on it, which is to listen in.

clue.text: Move schools, wanting one with further education? Right

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pupil changes schools in search of further education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' is a verb, 'trains'; 'wanting one' drops its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to move something or someone from one place to another.
